par-architecture-00.survivingClaim: Narrowed to the SDDP two-pass phase phrasing that genuinely encodes a single-engine assumption: 'forward/backward passes' (precompute.rs:11), 'forward pass' (lag_transition.rs:60), 'training/simulation lag transitions' (lag_transition.rs:137) and 'forward-pass hot path' (lag_transition.rs:160). par-over-engineering-00.survivingClaim: Narrowed: the confirmable residue is that all three bare forms have zero production callers (only crate tests + doctests exercise them) and estimate_ar_coefficients/estimate_seasonal_stats are additionally re-exported at the crate root (lib.rs:46-47) on top of the par::fitting:: path. par-over-engineering-01.survivingClaim: Narrowed: the fatal check inside validate_par_parameters (validation.rs:120, the zero-std/ar_order>0 error propagated by `?`) is live and load-bearing at context.rs:616 and must stay. par-performance-00.argument: Verified at baseline in correlation.rs: compute_seasonal_matrices (391) per season (a) clones each hydro's date-keyed residual map via `.cloned()` into season_residuals (line ~399), (b) computes min_pairs by walking all (i, i+1..n) pairs and intersecting the two date sets with contains_key (lines ~405-416), then (c) if min_pairs >= MIN_CORRELATION_PAIRS, calls compute_pearson_correlation_matrix (438) which re-walks the SAME pairs and re-intersects via r_j.get(&date) (lines ~448-453) and then pairs.sort_unstable_by date. Residuals are HashMap<NaiveDate,f64> built by compute_hydro_residuals (199), so each intersection re-hashes every date. So the pairwise date-overlap is computed twice per kept season and the layout pays a hash per element plus a per-pair sort. This is a real fitting-time redundancy. Per the brief's rayon-determinism mandate, any date-sorted-Vec fix MUST preserve compute_hydro_residuals' canonical hydro_ids-order collect (rationale at correlation.rs:205-208) and compute_pearson_correlation_matrix's NaiveDate-ordered accumulation (rationale at :434-438); NaiveDate is a total order within a series, so a sorted-Vec layout upholds both. Neutral: no engine noun, no dependency change.
par-performance-00.survivingClaim: Narrowed: the double date-set intersection holds only for seasons that pass the MIN_CORRELATION_PAIRS gate — a rejected season intersects once (in min_pairs) then `continue`s (correlation.rs:418-420), so it pays the walk once, not twice. And this is fitting/setup-time work (one correlation build per solve), so the confirmable cost is bounded setup latency and allocation traffic scaling with n_hydros^2 * observation-length, NOT a per-scenario/per-stage runtime-hot-path regression. Any fix must keep the two documented determinism contracts (canonical hydro_ids-order collect; NaiveDate-ordered pair accumulation) so declaration-order invariance is preserved.

par-performance-01.argument: Verified at baseline in estimation.rs: estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients (952, classical PACF path) fits every hydro under hydro_ids.par_iter().flat_map_iter(...).collect() (lines 952-965), while estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (the PAR(p)-A path) does the identical per-hydro shape — fresh per-iteration local vectors (obs_by_season/annual_obs_by_season/stats via clone_from + get) then per-season FACP/extended-YW solves pushed to a shared `estimates` Vec — inside a plain serial `for &hydro_id in hydro_ids` (line 397). Each annual iteration reads only immutable lookups (group_obs, annual_group_obs, stats_map, annual_stats_map, group_z_year_starts, annual_group_year_starts) and touches only its own hydro's seasons, so it is embarrassingly parallel in exactly the shape the classical site already exploits. The asymmetry is structural (one parallel, its byte-identical sibling serial). Per the brief's mandate, lifting it into par_iter().flat_map_iter().collect() MUST preserve the canonical hydro_ids reassembly documented at estimation.rs:947-951 so the estimates vector is produced in the same order the serial push yields — order-invariant and bit-identical. Neutral: no engine noun, no dependency change.
par-performance-01.survivingClaim: Narrowed: the parallelizable region is specifically the INITIAL per-hydro estimation loop of estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (the `for &hydro_id in hydro_ids { ... estimates.push(...) }` block starting estimation.rs:397), NOT the subsequent annual reduction (apply_annual_prepass_reductions / reduce_entity_orders_annual), which mutates `estimates` across hydro index sets and must remain serial in this change. It is a fitting/setup-time asymmetry (one fit per solve), and correctness requires the flat_map_iter/collect canonical hydro_ids-order reassembly (estimation.rs:947-951) so the result stays declaration-order-invariant.

par-performance-02.argument: Verified at baseline in estimation.rs: group_obs is a HashMap<(EntityId,usize),Vec<f64>> already owning each hydro-season's observations. Four consumers rebuild a local obs_by_season: Vec<Vec<f64>> via obs_by_season[season].clone_from(obs) (a full deep copy): the classical parallel closure estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients (line ~957-959), the serial reduce_entity_orders (~1066-1068), and in the PAR-A path estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (~406-408, cloning both group_obs and annual_group_obs) plus reduce_entity_orders_annual (~688-692, cloning both). Each then builds obs_refs: Vec<&[f64]> via .iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect() and passes borrows into the FACP/YW primitives; the owned copy exists only to derive that borrow view. Total observation bytes copied are 2x raw history for the classical fit (estimate + reduce) and up to 4x for PAR-A (Z + A across estimate + reduce). Constructing the borrow view directly from group_obs (which outlives every pass) removes the intermediate copy without changing any numeric result and leaves the classical closure's canonical hydro_ids-order collect untouched. Neutral: no engine noun, no dependency change.
par-performance-02.survivingClaim: Narrowed: the borrow-view substitution is valid only where the consumer never mutates the owned vector — verified true at the two reduction loops and the PAR-A initial estimate, which build obs_refs: Vec<&[f64]> and only read (e.g. the classical closure's `obs_by_season[season].len() < 2` guard reads, never writes). It is setup-time memory-traffic debt (one fit per solve), so the confirmable defect is bounded allocation/copy volume (2x classical / up to 4x PAR-A of raw history), NOT a per-iteration hot-path regression; and the classical par_iter closure's canonical hydro_ids-order collect (estimation.rs:947-951) is unaffected by swapping clone_from for a shared-immutable borrow.

par-test-bloat-00.argument: Verified at baseline: `diff` of tests.rs:1157-1168 (pop_mean_std) against tests.rs:2354-2365 (pop_mean_std_ann) yields a single differing line — the function name (`fn pop_mean_std` vs `fn pop_mean_std_ann`). sampling-architecture-00.argument: ClassSamplerParams.class_name is a bare &str (mod.rs:297) and build_class_sampler gates the Historical-only-for-inflow correctness rule on `if class_name != "inflow"` (mod.rs:436) — not merely diagnostics. Concede the two format!("historical_{class_name}")/format!("external_{class_name}") diagnostics and the broader entity_type string-matching in correlation/resolve.rs::apply_correlation_for_class are legitimate label/scan uses out of this candidate's scope.

sampling-architecture-01.argument: Verified at mod.rs:263-289: ForwardSamplerConfig is one flat #[derive(Copy)] bundle holding ctx: &StochasticContext (a persistent store whose own doc says it provides tree/seeds/correlation/entity-order — all generation-side artifacts) alongside four Option<&…Library> realized-value refs plus per-run class_schemes/stages/dims. build_forward_sampler (mod.rs:403) reads ONLY generation-side accessors off ctx (forward_seed/base_seed/entity_order/tree_view/correlation) while the four libraries are the realized-value inputs, so this is the single public sampling type spanning the generation/realized boundary with no type-level marker separating the two concerns. Concede that aggregating factory inputs behind one Copy struct is idiomatic and not a correctness bug, and that the scheme->library validity-coupling collapse is sibling oe-00's concern, not this one.
sampling-architecture-01.survivingClaim: The structural residue only: the four realized-value Option<&Library> fields share one flat Copy bundle with the &StochasticContext store handle and no type-level separation of the two concerns/lifetimes, so a reader of the seam cannot tell store from per-run input without reading build_forward_sampler's body — the store/param split the alignment epic should reshape (the shape that survives the Part IV/V Switchable<T> unification), not a runtime defect.

sampling-over-engineering-00.argument: Verified the derived-seed 4-tuple (derived_lag_values, l_state, derived_accum, derived_weight) is re-declared verbatim as positional params in standardize_external_inflow (external.rs:262), run_eta_inversion (eta_inversion.rs:37), standardize_historical_windows (historical.rs:296), and threaded further through build_external_inflow_library/build_historical_inflow_library/build_scenario_libraries in cobre-sddp (setup/scenario_libraries.rs, setup/mod.rs:1838). run_eta_inversion resets lag_state (from derived_lag_values), lag_accum (from derived_accum) and lag_weight_accum (from derived_weight) TOGETHER at every outer boundary (eta_inversion.rs:94-102), so they are operationally one seed — rebutting the #[allow] rationale's "no natural sub-grouping exists". I concede the rationale's "would just relocate the arity" clause: after bundling, standardize_external_inflow (11->8 args), standardize_historical_windows (13->10) and run_eta_inversion (13->10) all remain above clippy's 7-arg threshold, so #[allow(too_many_arguments)] is NOT eliminated and the candidate's "allow can be dropped" over-reaches.
sampling-over-engineering-00.survivingClaim: The rationale's "no natural sub-grouping exists" clause is false — the four are a documented atomic seed reset together at each outer boundary and re-threaded verbatim through >=6 signatures; the defensible residue is the silent same-typed transposition hazard between derived_accum and derived_weight (both &[f64], both length n_hydros, adjacent positional args) plus the reset-together invariant restated across >=3 doc blocks, which a by-ref DerivedSeed aggregate removes. The #[allow] itself stays (all three functions remain >7 args), so this is not an eliminate-the-lint finding.

sampling-over-engineering-01.argument: Verified at mod.rs:263-289 and build_class_sampler (mod.rs:317-388): the four Option<&Library> fields plus ClassSchemes' three scheme selectors encode a (3 class x scheme) validity matrix enforced only at runtime via StochasticError::MissingScenarioSource. build_forward_sampler hard-wires historical_library: None for both the load and ncs build sites, direct evidence the four Options are not independent knobs. The type admits scheme=External/Historical with the required Option None (a runtime-only error) and a library Some while the class scheme never reads it (silently-dead input), and the doc comments restate the coupling the type does not encode. Concede the runtime check is correct and emits a helpful diagnostic, so there is no live wrong-result bug — this is a representability / parse-don't-validate finding, not a correctness one.
sampling-over-engineering-01.survivingClaim: Representability only: the config permits exactly two invalid/redundant states — (a) a class scheme selects External/Historical but the paired Option is None (caught only at runtime), and (b) a library is Some while the class scheme never reads it (silent dead input) — and the hard-wired historical_library:None for load/ncs shows the four Options are not independent; folding each class's scheme+library into a per-class source enum makes both states unrepresentable. No claim of a runtime bug: the MissingScenarioSource check is correct today.

sampling-performance-00.argument: Verified class_sampler.rs:311 (OutOfSample fill) and out_of_sample.rs:63 are the only two production callers of fill_uncorrelated and both pass None for sobol_ctx; the git grep confirms scrambled_sobol_point_precomputed/SobolPrecomputed are referenced outside qmc_sobol/mod.rs ONLY in out_of_sample.rs (import + the Some branch at line 120), so that Some branch is never taken in production. scrambled_sobol_point rebuilds build_direction_matrix(dim) (Vec<[u32;32]>) and derive_scramble_params(seed, dim) (Vec<(u32,u32)>) every call; the seed is derive_opening_seed(sampling_seed, iteration, stage_id) with NO scenario term, so both are scenario-invariant at fixed (seed, iteration, stage, dim). SobolPrecomputed::new derives from the identical seed and scrambled_sobol_point_precomputed's per-scenario XOR/scramble math is identical, so wiring it is bit-for-bit deterministic. This is a real per-scenario recompute+heap-alloc on the forward hot path (CLAUDE.md: never allocate on hot paths).
sampling-performance-00.survivingClaim: Scoped to the OutOfSample QmcSobol forward path only (SAA/InSample/Historical/External are allocation-free per the positives): the direction matrix + scramble params are recomputed and heap-allocated per (iteration, scenario, stage) though invariant across the scenario axis, and the existing SobolPrecomputed/sobol_ctx seam already amortizes this bit-identically — so the residue is wiring an existing dormant hoist whose sole production caller hard-codes None, not new infrastructure and not a determinism risk.

sampling-performance-01.argument: Verified sample_lhs_point (tree/lhs.rs): for each of `dim` output slots it re-initializes perm[0..n] (n = total_scenarios) and runs a full fisher_yates over n, then reads only perm[scenario_idx]. perm_rng is seeded from derive_opening_seed(sampling_seed, iteration, stage_id) with NO scenario term — the in-code comment 'perm_rng advances identically on all workers, so the permutation matches' confirms scenario-invariance — so the same `dim` permutations are recomputed for every scenario. Called once per scenario (class_sampler.rs:311 OutOfSample fill), per-stage cost is O(dim*total_scenarios^2) where O(dim*total_scenarios) suffices. draw_rng is per-(scenario,dimension) so stratified values stay distinct, and a per-(iteration,stage) permutation cache preserves bit-for-bit output because perm_seed is unchanged.
sampling-performance-01.survivingClaim: Scoped to the OutOfSample LHS forward path, and a redundant-COMPUTE finding (not allocation — perm_scratch is caller-owned): the scenario-invariant set of `dim` Fisher-Yates permutations of `total_scenarios` strata is reshuffled once per scenario, giving the quadratic-in-scenario O(dim*total_scenarios^2) per stage that a per-(iteration,stage) permutation cache (or the existing generate_lhs batch primitive) collapses to O(dim*total_scenarios), determinism preserved.

sampling-performance-02.argument: Verified scrambled_halton_point (qmc_halton/mod.rs:261): per call it runs sieve_primes(spec.dim) (allocates a Vec sieve then collects a Vec<u32>) and build_scramble_tables(seed, &primes, total_scenarios) returning a nested Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>>, then reads one point per dim. The seed is derive_opening_seed(sampling_seed, iteration, stage_id) with NO scenario term, so primes+tables are scenario-invariant at fixed (seed, iteration, stage, dim, total_scenarios) yet freshly heap-allocated and recomputed for every scenario draw (class_sampler.rs:311 OutOfSample fill). This is both a hot-path allocation storm (CLAUDE.md: never allocate on hot paths) and redundant table construction. Confirmed via grep there is no HaltonPrecomputed type or halton_ctx seam (unlike Sobol), so the primitive must be added in the tree-noise cell.
sampling-performance-02.survivingClaim: Scoped to the OutOfSample QmcHalton forward path: the per-scenario fresh prime-sieve + nested Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>> scramble-table allocation and recomputation is scenario-invariant and should be hoisted per (iteration, stage); because NO HaltonPrecomputed seam exists (unlike Sobol's dormant one), the precompute primitive is a cross-station dependency on the tree-noise cell and only the sampler-side wiring is this sub-station's part; determinism is preserved (tables are a pure function of the existing seed tuple).
